items.explanation: 71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with chart diagnosis of atrial fibrillation. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14).

A 12-lead ECG (104882441) was obtained on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met.

CHA2DS2-VASc 5: hypertension, age 65-74, prior ischaemic stroke (cerebral infarction / embolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis), female sex. Current clinic medications at the last visit (2026-07-10) are carvedilol, famotidine and metoprolol tartrate; there is no anticoagulant order, active or documented. Anticoagulation is recommended and absent.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused), with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic visit re-ordered and listed apixaban 5 mg twice daily as a current medication (together with aspirin and clopidogrel), so an anticoagulant is being continued without the documented review.

At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started to replace rivaroxaban for insurance reasons, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered at the same visit and both drugs are listed as current medications. Two oral anticoagulants (apixaban and rivaroxaban) are therefore concurrently active; the rivaroxaban order was never stopped.

Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves at a ventricular rate of about 143-144/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings.

The sinus-rhythm entry is contradicted by the same-day ECG.

Compared with 2025-06-07 (108780865, sinus with marked cycle-length variation, QTc ~440 ms) the QTc has risen by about 100 ms, in keeping with the amiodarone started 2025-11-10; flagged for prescriber review.

Compared with 2025-06-07 (108780865, sinus with marked cycle-length variation, QTc ~440 ms) the QTc has risen by about 100 ms, in keeping with the amiodarone started 2025-11-10; flagged for prescriber review.

items.explanation: 71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with chart diagnosis of atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease: coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). Current clinic medication list as of the last visit (2026-07-28) is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily only; no oral anticoagulant is ordered or active. Guideline-recommended anticoagulation is absent.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, most recent clinic order 2026-08-22) with warfarin. Most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 61/min with frequent ventricular ectopy and a very long QT of about 552 ms, Bazett QTc about 560 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG (104882441) was obtained on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10. The 9/1/2025 memo applies (start before 3/1/2026), requiring an ECG within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met (that ECG also showed QTc >500 ms and is flagged separately).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start precedes 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Started on or after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo required an ECG within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded on 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window; no qualifying ECG was obtained by the due date, which has passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (not present on the med list at the 2026-06-24 visit). The revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The patient's only ECG is from 2025-12-25, before the start; no ECG has been obtained since, and the due date has passed.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. The revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracings are from March 2025), but the window is still open as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so the revised memo required an ECG within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart. However, the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a clinician dose change, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD, acting under the clinic standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily for a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change; no INR has been drawn since, and the due date has passed.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0). CHA2DS2-VASc 5: hypertension, age 65-74, prior ischaemic stroke (cerebral infarction / embolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis), female sex. Current clinic medications at the last visit (2026-07-10) are carvedilol, famotidine and metoprolol tartrate; there is no anticoagulant order, active or documented. Anticoagulation is recommended and absent.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused), with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic visit re-ordered and listed apixaban 5 mg twice daily as a current medication (together with aspirin and clopidogrel), so an anticoagulant is being continued without the documented review.

At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started to replace rivaroxaban for insurance reasons, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered at the same visit and both drugs are listed as current medications. Two oral anticoagulants (apixaban and rivaroxaban) are therefore concurrently active; the rivaroxaban order was never stopped.

The 2026-06-10 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves at a ventricular rate of about 143-144/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings.

The 12-lead ECG obtained the same day at 06:30 (100867733) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at about 129/min with absent P waves (atrial fibrillation), and the rhythm entry four minutes earlier (06:34) records 'Atrial Fibrillation'. The sinus-rhythm entry is contradicted by the same-day ECG.

His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 482 ms and Bazett QTc 514 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2025-08-23) are normal.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, most recent clinic order 2026-07-29) with warfarin. Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with a markedly prolonged QT (about 530 ms) giving a Bazett QTc of roughly 540 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal.

Patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, most recent clinic order 2026-05-29). Most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT about 495 ms and Bazett QTc about 535 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required (citalopram 40 mg also exceeds the usual maximum for QT risk). Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal.
